subject: Channel crediting structure for Azure Private Offer: list-price floor & uplift mechanics
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Azure Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@microsoft.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure PO mechanics - list price floor + partner uplift question

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at AcmeCorp is interested in moving forward with a 12–18 month commit for Redwood via an Azure Private Offer. Before we lock term/commit we need clarity on how Redwood proposes to handle: list-price floor on the marketplace listing vs net price we charge, and how channel uplift/credits flow to our reseller (NorthPoint). A few specifics: 

- We want to keep the marketplace listing price at a published level for procurement consistency, but NorthPoint needs an explicit channel credit so their margin viability is preserved.
- Will Redwood be able to pay a rebate/credit to the partner if Azure invoices show the full marketplace list price?
- Do marketplace fees (Microsoft take) affect how you structure credits?

Estimate: $120k ARR committed (first year usage ~ $95k). Partner needs a ~18% margin on ARR to participate.

Can you outline your recommended structure and whether the credit can be applied without changing the public list price? Also include timing (monthly/quarterly) and how we handle invoicing for the PO.

Thanks,
Sasha Patel
VP Procurement, AcmeCorp
</sasha.patel@acmecorp.com>

Attachments: none

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Azure Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@microsoft.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure PO mechanics - list price floor + partner uplift question

Hi Sasha,

Appreciate the clarity — excited to get this over the line. High-level options (short):

Option A — External credit (recommended for compliance + accounting simplicity)
- Keep marketplace list price as the committed gross list on Azure (no change).
- Redwood issues a separate channel credit to NorthPoint, expressed as a rebate/credit applied by Redwood to AcmeCorp's monthly invoice (off-platform).
- Channel credit percentage (example): target 18% of net ARR. If net ARR equals $95k for year 1, credit budget = $17,100.
- Timing: monthly reconciliation and credit applied within 30 days of invoice. Payouts are internal Redwood credits (not a third-party cash pass-through).
- Marketplace fees: Microsoft transaction fees remain on the gross invoice — Redwood credit is a separate accounting item and does not reduce the marketplace invoice.

Option B — List-price passback (less recommended)
- Adjust marketplace list price upward to include partner uplift, then Redwood issues a buyer-facing discount so partner margin is preserved on the invoice flow.
- This complicates tax/finance and requires marketplace ops coordination. It also can affect procurement approval workflows.

Pros/cons: Option A keeps Azure procurement intact and avoids modifying listing metadata; Option B is cleaner for partner cash flow but creates complexity on marketplace reconciliation and tax.

I've attached a simple calc (azure_po_channel_credit_calc.xlsx) with the $95k net example showing monthly accruals vs quarterly reconciliation and a PDF with the proposed credit flow.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm partner legal (NorthPoint) is comfortable receiving Redwood credits applied to the invoice vs direct cash.
2) Ben, can you confirm the tax implications and whether we should structure credit as a credit memo or partner rebate (Irene, tagging you for compliance/input)?
3) If OK, we'll draft the PO language that preserves the list price and references Redwood crediting terms.

Happy to jump on a short call with Acme and NorthPoint if helpful.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: azure_po_channel_credit_calc.xlsx, channel_credit_flow.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Acme / NorthPoint - channel credit math and execution path

Ben/Irene —
Quick internal sync before I circle back to Sasha. Key points and asks: 

- Acme commits ~$120k ARR list; our estimate of delivered net is $95k (after usage profile / discounts). Partner needs ~18% margin (~$17.1k).
- Proposal: Redwood issues monthly credits to Acme's invoice as a Redwood-issued credit memo that is designated to NorthPoint per the partner agreement. This keeps the Azure marketplace list price intact.

Questions: 
- Ben: Do we treat these credits as contra-revenue or partner marketing credit for accounting? Impact on revenue recognition? Quick call with finance may be needed.
- Irene: Any compliance restrictions for routing a Redwood credit to satisfy partner margin when the marketplace invoice is handled by Microsoft? Specifically: KYC for partner payout path and whether we need partner onboarding docs.

Also: if Microsoft requires the listing price to be representative for procurement, we should avoid list-price gymnastics. Option A from my outbound is the low-friction route.

If we agree, I will:
- Draft PO language that states: "Marketplace list price will remain unchanged; Redwood will provide partner crediting to NorthPoint per the attached schedule. Credits are issued monthly as Redwood credit memos and netted on Redwood invoices."
- Ask Acme to confirm NorthPoint as the recipient of the credit and get partner contact + W-9/PO details.

Available 1pm today if you want to jump on a quick alignment.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure PO mechanics - list price floor + partner uplift question

Thanks for the clear write-up, Dylan and Sasha — this approach is workable from finance ops with the following clarifications and next steps:

- Accounting treatment: We will record Redwood-issued partner credits as a contra-revenue credit memo tied to the Acme contract. That preserves gross invoicing for marketplace reporting while giving the partner their uplift via a Redwood credit application. We will work with Acme's AP team to apply the credit to monthly invoices.

- Tax and marketplace fees: Microsoft retains marketplace fees on their invoice. Our credit does not reduce the reported marketplace gross for Microsoft. From Redwood's perspective, the credit reduces recognized revenue via contra-revenue. Tax impact is minimal for Redwood but please note partners should seek their own tax advice.

- List-price floor: To address procurement requirements, we recommend a published list price that is no less than 10% above expected net pricing. Practically we can set a list-price floor of +10% and keep the credit mechanism for partner margin rather than inflating list price to match partner uplift.

- Execution items:
  1) Sasha: Please confirm NorthPoint contact + vendor tax docs (W-9 or equivalent).
  2) Dylan: I will prepare a template credit memo and routing instructions for AP reconciliation.
  3) Irene: Please confirm compliance checklist for partner KYC and whether a short addendum is required for marketplace reporting.

I attached the calc with contra-revenue line items updated per our approach. Once Sasha confirms so we can finalize PO language and route DocuSign.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
